title: Empire's Trump Card
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji fell into contemplation, an unusual wind sound suddenly came through the window—that was the message crane bell exclusively used by the imperial envoy...

text.content: Chen Ji's fingertip hovered above the activation mark, his pupils reflecting a massive chessboard covering the entire continent. Black and white pieces interlaced纵横, and he himself—along with his long-missing sister Chen Nian—were merely two pieces about to be captured on the board. That feeling of being completely seen through made his back chill, as if a pair of eyes beyond the mortal world were watching all his arrangements.

dialogue.content:
"Did you see it?"

A faint green ghostly light slowly emerged from the Tianji Record Fragment at Chen Ji's chest, Mo Xiansheng's aged and illusory face flickering in the moonlight. "That is not an illusion, but the deepest memory within the Tianji Record—every successor throughout the ages has seen the same scene."

His voice was low and weary, carrying a subtle, barely perceptible sadness.

text.content:
Chen Ji withdrew his finger, his expression terrifyingly calm: "I thought I was the chess master."

Mo Xiansheng drifted closer, his illusory form passing through the window lattice, moonlight falling on his tattered Taoist robe: "You think laying out the world, having every calculation accounted for makes one a chess master? Child, we are merely pieces chosen to push the chess game forward."

These words struck Chen Ji's heart like an invisible blade.

dialogue.content:
"Then who is the true chess master?"

Chen Ji's voice was soft, as if squeezed from between his teeth, yet the flames of fury burning in his eyes had already revealed his state of mind. What he hated most in life was being treated as a piece—whether abandoned by the sect in his youth or now discovering he was merely a chess piece in a grander scheme.

Mo Xiansheng remained silent for a moment before speaking slowly:

"Cang Yutian."

The weight of these three characters seemed to press down like a thousand tons. Mo Xiansheng's illusory form trembled slightly: "The founder of the Imperial Dynasty, the man hailed as the emperor of ten thousand ages. Do you know how he came to be?"

Chen Ji's brow furrowed slightly: "Legend says he was once mortal, stumbled upon a secret manual in ancient ruins, and rose through the ranks—"

"Legend?" Mo Xiansheng let out a desolate laugh. "That is merely a script written for mortals to read."

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng's illusory form drifted to the window, gazing at the pale moon in the distant sky: "Five thousand years ago, the Heavenly Will first descended with a divine decree, searching the world for a human vessel capable of bearing its will. Countless geniuses were screened, countless powerhouses were eliminated, and in the end—only one body met the conditions."

He turned around, a complex light flickering in his turbid eyes: "That was Cang Yutian. He was not a naturally powerful emperor, but a tool selected and meticulously shaped by the Heavenly Will."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji suddenly smiled.

The smile was faint, yet carried an inexplicable chill: "So the imperial authority, the Five Great Sects, the Demonic Path Alliance... all are pieces arranged by the Heavenly Will?"

"It is more terrifying than that." Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly dropped lower, "The Heavenly Will is not a singular existence; it is composed of countless fragmented consciousnesses. What resides within Cang Yutian is merely the tip of the iceberg. And each fragment is seeking more vessels—"

His gaze fell meaningfully on the Tianji Record Fragment at Chen Ji's chest.

text.content:
Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply.

He instinctively covered his chest—the fragment was now hot as a piece of fresh iron from the furnace. He suddenly understood—why the Tianji Record was fragmented, why each use consumed Heavenly Fate Value, why Mo Xiansheng could only exist as a remnant soul.

All of this was to prevent him from becoming too powerful, lest he threaten the Heavenly Will's arrangements.

dialogue.content:
"The Tianji Record was originally part of the Heavenly Will." Mo Xiansheng said slowly, "It was divided into countless fragments scattered across the mortal world, each page containing the ability to glimpse heavenly secrets. But if someone could gather all the fragments—"

He did not finish, but Chen Ji had already understood.

That would be power capable of standing in opposition to the Heavenly Will.

Chen Ji lowered his gaze, his voice terrifyingly calm: "So what about Chen Nian? Was she taken by the Holy Sect because of this too?"

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng's illusory form trembled slightly—this was the first time he had shown a shaken expression before Chen Ji.

After a long while, he spoke: "Chen Nian's bloodline is very special. She is the only existence capable of interfering with the Tianji Record's foresight. Any prophecy that involves her appears blurred."

His voice grew low: "What the Heavenly Will fears is never you alone, but the two of you together. If you and Chen Nian become one—"

Before he could finish, a sharp whistling sound suddenly came through the window.

choice.prompt: Facing this sudden turn of events, Chen Ji had to make a choice:

choices.text: Immediately pursue the source of the whistling sound
choices.description: The sound came menacingly, certainly nothing good. Chen Ji had to gain intelligence第一时间, to judge how the next move should be made.

text.content:
Chen Ji's figure flashed, turning into a shadow and dashing toward the window. Under the moonlight, three black silhouettes were rushing from the distance. The leader wore a dark-patterned cloak of the imperial envoy, holding a completely black jade box in his hands.

That was the message box exclusively used by the Imperial Sovereign—inside was some kind of earth-shaking command.

choices.description: Mo Xiansheng is one of Chen Ji's biggest trump cards and must not be easily exposed. First ensure his safety, then face the enemy at leisure.
choices.visible_reward: Preserve Mo Xiansheng as a hidden card
choices.risk_hint: The arrivals may be here for Mo Xiansheng

choices.text: Activate Tianji Record to foresee three hours
choices.description: Before making any decision, Chen Ji needs to first see what will happen in the next three hours. This is the safest choice.

text.content: Chen Ji quietly activated the foresight ability of the Tianji Record. Instantly, countless images flooded into his mind like a tide— the imperial envoy, the emperor's secret order, even a vague, otherworldly gaze. But strangely, at the edge of all these visions, Chen Nian's figure was shrouded in a hazy mist, impossible to see clearly. Mo Xiansheng was right—Chen Nian's very existence was interference to the Tianji Record.

Three black shadows fell into the courtyard. The leader was a cold-faced middle-aged man with unfathomable aura—at least a peak Transformed God realm expert. "Chen Ji?" The man glanced at Chen Ji standing by the window, a disdainful smile curling his lips, "The famoustrash disciple of Tianqing Sect, truly not an overstatement. Admiring the moon at this late hour—quite the leisurely mood." The two attendants behind him let out low snickers.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji bowed slightly, assuming a terrified expression: "I wonder what brings the esteemed officials to visit so late at night? This humble servant disciple is merely..." "Enough." The middle-aged man impatiently cut him off, taking out a bright yellow silk scroll from his chest, "This is the emperor's secret order. Chen Ji, three days later, you will represent Tianqing Sect and accompany us to the imperial capital for an audience with His Majesty." His gaze was like looking at an ant: "This is an honor, understand?"

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his head, hands trembling as he received the silk scroll. But his heart was ice-cold. An audience with the emperor in three days? This was no coincidence—the Tianji Record had just revealed the existence of Heavenly Will, and now the empire sent people to summon him to the capital. The connection between these events was almost self-evident. He might be being led into a pre-designed trap. But perhaps—this was an opportunity to get closer to the core truth.

dialogue.content: At that moment, a voice only Chen Ji could hear rang in his mind. Mo Xiansheng's voice was unusually grave: "Be careful. Cang Yutian has lived for five thousand years, but he cannot truly be immortal. Heavenly Will needs a vessel, and vessels always decay in time..." He didn't finish, but Chen Ji already understood his subtext. The emperor's summons might not be for reward, but—for a new vessel.

choice.prompt: Facing the imperial envoy's arrogance and the emperor's secret order, Chen Ji needs to respond:

choices.text: Pretend to be overwhelmed with gratitude and accept
choices.description: Accept the order with the proper attitude of atrash disciple full of gratitude, without arousing any suspicion, and plan secretly.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily endure humiliation and bide time
choices.risk_hint: May be seen as weak and easily bullied

dialogue.content: Chen Ji thudded to his knees, voice trembling: "I... how do I, a mere nobody, deserve the emperor's favor! This is my ancestors' grave exhaling smoke, a fortune accumulated over eight lifetimes!" His forehead pressed tightly against the cold stone slab, shoulders slightly quivering, perfectly portraying a overwhelmed fool. The middle-aged man snorted coldly: "Smart of you. At the third hour on the third day, be at the city gate."

choices.description: 以废材的curious心probing皇主召见的具体原因，看能否套出更多情报。

dialogue.content: Chen Ji raised his head, asking with innocent curiosity: "Um... if I may be so bold, may I ask why His Majesty wishes to summon someone like me, atrash? This subordinate has never left the sect, afraid of offending noble guests..." A strange glint flashed in the middle-aged man's eyes, then returned to cold indifference: "Don't ask what you shouldn't. Just know that this is the emperor's grace." He turned to leave but paused, whispering: "By the way, the emperor specially ordered—if there are companions, they are strictly prohibited from accompanying."

text.content: The three black shadows vanished into the night sky like escaping light, leaving only Chen Ji standing by the window, the bright yellow silk scroll in his hand gleaming with a bizarre luster under the moonlight. Chen Ji slowly straightened up, the timidity and terror on his face like a mask being peeled away, replaced by an unfathomable calm. "Heavenly Will... Cang Yutian..." he murmured these two names, his lips suddenly curling into a cold smile, "Interesting."

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng's phantom appeared again, his gaze falling on the silk scroll in Chen Ji's hand, silent for a long while before speaking. "What do you plan to do?" Chen Ji didn't answer but unfolded the scroll, carefully examining its contents under the moonlight. Suddenly, his brow furrowed slightly. "Mo Xiansheng, look here—" he pointed to an inconspicuous mark in the corner of the scroll, "This rune... I've seen it on a certain page of the Tianji Record." Mo Xiansheng's phantom suddenly froze, his turbid eyes flickering with a flash of horror.

text.content:
"This is... the Mark of Heavenly Fate." Mo Xiansheng's voice trembled slightly. "Only those who have been directly touched by the Heavenly Will would bear such a mark on their body."

Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply.

He lowered his head to look at his hands—under the moonlight, nothing was visible. But since Mo Xiansheng could recognize this mark, its existence could not be false.

In other words, Cang Yutian had marked him long before summoning him?

When was he touched? And in what manner?

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng meditated for a moment, then suddenly said, "Chen Ji, think carefully—before you obtained the Tianji Record Fragment, had you encountered anything unusual? Or... had any strange dreams?"

Chen Ji closed his eyes, and memories surged back like a tide to that night many years ago.

That was the place where he first found the Fragment—beside the dried well at the Rear Mountain of the sect. At that time, the Fragment was wrapped inside a peculiar jade stone, and that jade stone...

His eyes snapped open: "The jade stone!"

text.content:
Chen Ji's voice carried a barely perceptible tremor: "That jade stone that wrapped the Fragment—I always thought it was just an ordinary container. But if—"

"What if that jade stone itself is part of the Heavenly Will?" Mo Xiansheng interjected, his voice carrying a hint of bitterness. "The moment you touched it, you had already formed a connection with the Heavenly Will. The Fragment recognizing you as its master afterward was only natural."

Chen Ji suddenly laughed.

That smile was cold and sharp, carrying a transcendent air of having seen through everything: "So I was never a lucky one chosen by the Tianji Record, but rather a Chess Game set in motion years ago?"

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng did not answer, but his silence was itself an answer.

After a long while, he slowly spoke: "But this also means something else—the Heavenly Will chose you because there is something within you that it needs. Whatever this quality may be, you are not a puppet to be manipulated."

His phantom drifted closer to Chen Ji, and a rare seriousness flashed in his murky eyes: "Remember, child. A true Chess Player never lets the chess piece know it is being manipulated. And now that you have perceived it—there remains a chance to break the game."

choice.prompt: Faced with the truth of being a "chosen chess piece," how should Chen Ji respond?

choices.text: Accept fate but refuse to surrender
choices.description: Since he is already a piece, let him be an unruly one. Since he was chosen, it proves he has value worth choosing—let him use this value to shake the chessboard itself.
choices.visible_cost: Lie dormant in the early stage
choices.visible_reward: Receive further guidance from Mo Xiansheng
choices.risk_hint: May fall into an even deeper trap

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, the gloom on his face swept away, replaced by an almost manic determination.

"Mo Xiansheng." He stared directly at Mo Xiansheng's phantom. "You said that with each completed volume objective, a page of knowledge would be unsealed. Now tell me—what is the core objective of the next volume?"

Mo Xiansheng smiled faintly, and the phantom actually emanated a sense of gratification: "Good, you've finally asked the right question."

choices.text: Immediately begin investigating the Mark of Heavenly Fate
choices.description: Since he already bears the Mark of Heavenly Fate on his body, it is both the greatest weakness and the biggest clue. Chen Ji must understand the mark's function and how to use or escape it.
choices.risk_hint: Disturb the grass and alert the snake

text.content:
Chen Ji drew a silver needle from his怀, turning it slowly under the moonlight.

"Mo Xiansheng, this Mark of Heavenly Fate could be hidden anywhere within my body. To thoroughly investigate, I need to employ the power of the Tianji Record to trace the mark's source from within."

Mo Xiansheng reflected for a moment: "This is very dangerous. If the Heavenly Will senses you investigating it—"

"Then let it sense." Chen Ji interrupted him, dangerous light flickering in his eyes. "I want to know what this 'Chess Player' of mine is truly worth."

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng's phantom gazed at Chen Ji for a long while, then suddenly let out a soft sigh.

"Five hundred years ago, I also asked the same question." His voice became distant and ethereal. "Back then, I thought that as long as I was strong enough, I could break free from fate's shackles. Later, I discovered—"

He raised his phantom palm, casting a faint shadow under the moonlight: "Power is never the answer. The true key lies not on the chessboard, but in the heart of the Chess Player."

As his words fell, his figure began to slowly fade away.

text.content:
"Wait!" Chen Ji called out to him. "What does this mean? In the heart of the Chess Player—"

Mo Xiansheng's figure had faded to near invisibility, leaving only an ethereal voice echoing in the night wind.

"In three days, enter the capital, and you will find your answer. Remember—before those eyes gaze upon you, first learn to see your own heart."

The last wisp of remnant soul merged into the Fragment, the Tianji Record Fragment suddenly burning hot, then falling silent.

Chen Ji stood by the window, gazing at the empty courtyard, long silent.

Moonlight fell upon his face, outlining a visage both familiar and unfamiliar.

Chen Ji lowered his gaze to his hands—in these very hands, he held an imperial secret decree, a mark from the Heavenly Will, and a seemingly inescapable fate.

But he was Chen Ji.

The Chen Ji who crawled out from the pile of refuse.

The Chen Ji who calculated every move and advanced methodically.

He lightly clenched his fist, a cold smile curving his lips: "A chess piece on the board... is that it?"

"Fine. Then let the Chess Player see just how big a wave this piece can stir."

The night wind suddenly rose violently, rattling the window lattice.

Chen Ji turned and walked back inside, carefully tucking that bright yellow silk scroll into his怀. His movements were light and steady, as if merely storing an ordinary item.

But in the instant he bent down, a sharp light flickered across his eyes.

Three days.

He had three days to prepare for a game that might shake the entire continent.

But before that—there was still one thing he must confirm.

He produced a communication jade talisman, quietly infusing a thread of spiritual energy. The talisman glowed faintly, then transformed into an invisible rune that pierced through the night sky.
